subject: Introduction to Psychology (MIT 9.00SC, Fall 2011)
goal: Deep, MIT-level foundation in psychology as a first rung toward eventually practicing it professionally.
learner_prior: Everyday intuitive mind-reading — already predicts, explains, and is sometimes wrong about other people's behavior.

cruxes.title: Psychology as a Science
cruxes.hook: You already predict people all day. Why does it go wrong — and what would it take to do it on purpose?
cruxes.owns: Everyday intuitive mind-reading (the learner's starting prior)

cruxes.title: The Biological Machine
cruxes.hook: If behavior needs a testable cause, what is doing the causing underneath?
cruxes.owns: Behavior needs a falsifiable, testable cause (from 01)

cruxes.title: Perception Is Construction, Not Recording
cruxes.hook: Your eyes send the brain a blurry, upside-down, twitchy signal. How do you ever see anything?
cruxes.owns: Neurons and brain organization as the physical substrate (from 02)

cruxes.title: Attention & Consciousness
cruxes.hook: If perception builds a whole world for you, why can you still miss a gorilla walking through it?

cruxes.title: Learning
cruxes.hook: A dog hears a bell and starts drooling. What did it actually learn?
cruxes.owns: Attention as the gate on what gets processed (from 04)

cruxes.title: Memory
cruxes.hook: If learning rewires you, where does the rewiring live — and why does memory lie to you?
cruxes.owns: Learning as durable change in the organism (from 05)

cruxes.title: Language & Thought
cruxes.hook: Memory stores pieces. How do you assemble them into a sentence — or a decision?
cruxes.owns: Memory as reconstruction from stored pieces (from 06)

cruxes.title: Intelligence
cruxes.hook: If thinking has machinery, can one number capture how good someone's machinery is?

cruxes.title: Emotion
cruxes.hook: Your heart races before you know you're afraid. So what is a feeling actually made of?
cruxes.owns: Reasoning/appraisal (from 08) meeting the body's alarm system (from 02)

cruxes.title: Personality
cruxes.hook: Why does the same situation make one friend furious and another amused?
cruxes.owns: Emotion as a personal response pattern (from 09)

cruxes.title: Development Across the Lifespan
cruxes.hook: None of this — memory, emotion, personality — showed up fully formed. How does it get built, and does it ever stop?
cruxes.owns: Personality as a stable individual pattern (from 10), now asking how stable patterns form

cruxes.title: Stress & Health
cruxes.hook: You've grown a whole mind. Now watch what happens to it — and your body — under sustained threat.
cruxes.owns: A developed mind that can be pushed off balance (from 11)

cruxes.title: Psychopathology
cruxes.hook: Everyone gets stressed, sad, anxious. So where's the line — is there one — between that and a disorder?
cruxes.owns: The stress response pushed past what it can absorb (from 12)

cruxes.title: Social Psychology
cruxes.hook: You've built an entire theory of one mind. Drop it in a room with other minds — does it still predict behavior?
cruxes.owns: Everything so far, now tested against situational forces (from 13)

cruxes.title: Synthesis: What the Whole Course Was
cruxes.hook: Fourteen topics, one throughline. What is the whole course, shrunk back to what's irreducible?
cruxes.owns: All prior rungs, integrated back to behavior + empiricism (from 14)
